title: Minimum Absolute Sum Difference
summary: Given two arrays of positive integers, nums1 and nums2 of equal length, calculate the minimum possible absolute sum difference after replacing at most one element in nums1.
statement: Given two arrays of positive integers, nums1 and nums2 of equal length, calculate the minimum possible absolute sum difference after replacing at most one element in nums1. The absolute sum difference is the sum of the absolute differences between corresponding elements. The result is returned modulo 10^9 + 7. The absolute value |x| is the non-negative value of x.
constraints: Arrays have equal positive length; one nums1 element may be replaced by any value already present in nums1.
Minimize the total absolute pairwise difference and return it modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: For each target nums2 value, find the closest value available in nums1.
Sort a copy of nums1 and use binary search around every nums2 value.
Compute the largest reduction from replacing one original pair, then subtract it from the initial sum.
Only one index changes, so gains are independent; predecessor and successor around the insertion point are the closest legal replacements.
editorial: Only one index changes, so gains are independent; predecessor and successor around the insertion point are the closest legal replacements.

tests.explanation: Replacing seven by one or five reduces the sum to three.
The arrays already match, so no replacement is needed.
